skill.name: codebase-analysis
skill.description: Analyze project structure, dependencies, architecture, code quality, and security signals to help teams understand a codebase.
skill.summary: Creates a structured codebase analysis report covering stack, architecture, quality, dependencies, and next steps.
skill.author: AI-Vibe-Prompts

security_audit.summary: Most static command findings are false positives caused by Markdown inline code or fenced examples, not executable Ruby backticks. I confirmed the npm script instructions, package-manager audit and outdated commands, and .env scanning guidance as real risks because they can execute repository-controlled code, contact registries, or expose secrets. No prompt-injection text was found in SKILL.md.

remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user approval before running npm run lint or npm run test:coverage, and mark these checks as optional for unknown repositories.
Do not read real .env files. Detect only their presence, prefer .env.example, and redact values if the user explicitly requests inspection.
Ask before running npm audit, pnpm audit, or npm outdated, and explain that these commands may contact package registries.
Disable auto_invoke or split command-running steps into a separate opt-in phase after passive codebase discovery completes.

static_findings.snippet: 1. **Identify project type** by reading `package.json`, `tsconfig.json`, or framework-specific confi
- Next.js: Check for `next` in dependencies, `next.config.*`, `app/` or `pages/` directory
- Run linter if available: `npm run lint` (via Bash)
- Find test files: Use Glob for `**/*.{test,spec}.{js,ts,jsx,tsx}`
- Calculate coverage: Run `npm run test:coverage` if available
- `quality-gates` - Use analysis results to run appropriate quality checks
- `project-initialization` - Compare against templates to identify missing setup
- Framework-specific skills (`nextjs-optimization`, `react-patterns`) - Auto-invoke based on detecte

content.value_statement: Teams need a fast way to understand unfamiliar repositories before changing them. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through structure, dependency, architecture, quality, and security checks.
actual_capabilities: Maps root directories and key project files.
Identifies frameworks, package managers, dependencies, and build tools.
Reviews architecture patterns for components, APIs, state, and file organization.
Checks quality signals such as linting, tests, TypeScript settings, and common debt markers.
Summarizes security and dependency signals from lock files and package audit commands.
Produces a Markdown report with recommendations, risk areas, and next steps.
limitations: It depends on file access provided by the host AI tool.
Large repositories may need targeted analysis by directory.
Package audit and test coverage commands can be slow or unavailable.
It should avoid reading real environment secret files.

use_cases.title: Onboard to an Existing Repository
use_cases.description: Create a concise map of the project type, main folders, dependencies, and first risks before feature work starts.

use_cases.title: Plan a Refactor
use_cases.description: Identify architecture patterns, quality gaps, test coverage signals, and likely risk areas before changing shared code.

use_cases.title: Prepare a Technical Review
use_cases.description: Summarize stack choices, dependency health, security signals, and technical debt for a time-boxed repository assessment.

prompt_templates.title: Quick Repository Overview
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner request for a first-pass project map.
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this repository and summarize its project type, main directories, technologies, and first risks. Do not run package scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Architecture Review
prompt_templates.scenario: Intermediate review before planning a larger change.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review the architecture of this codebase. Identify component patterns, API structure, state management, file organization, and areas that need closer inspection.

prompt_templates.title: Quality and Dependency Assessment
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of maintainability and dependency signals.
prompt_templates.prompt: Assess code quality, linting setup, tests, TypeScript strictness, dependency freshness, and known vulnerability signals. Ask before running commands that execute project scripts.

prompt_templates.title: Refactoring Readiness Audit
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced targeted analysis for a planned refactor.
prompt_templates.prompt: Perform a targeted codebase analysis for this module or path. Map dependencies, ownership boundaries, risky files, test gaps, and a staged refactor plan.

output_examples.input: Analyze a Next.js app before feature work.
output_examples.output: A report naming the framework, app structure, key libraries, test status, quality risks, and recommended first fixes.

output_examples.input: Review a repository for refactoring readiness.
output_examples.output: A prioritized summary of architecture patterns, coupling risks, missing tests, technical debt, and safe next steps.

output_examples.input: Assess dependency and security signals in a frontend project.
output_examples.output: A concise dependency overview with package manager, lock file status, audit command guidance, outdated package signals, and review cautions.

best_practices: Start with metadata and directory structure before reading implementation files.
Ask for approval before running package scripts or audit commands.
Redact secrets and prefer environment examples over real secret files.
anti_patterns: Reading every file in a large repository before forming a plan.
Running repository scripts automatically in an untrusted project.
Treating dependency audit output as complete security coverage.

faq.question: What does this skill analyze?
faq.answer: It analyzes project structure, technology stack, architecture patterns, quality signals, dependency status, and next steps.

faq.question: Can it run tests or linters?
faq.answer: It can suggest those commands, but users should approve package script execution before it runs in an untrusted repository.

faq.question: Does it support large repositories?
faq.answer: Yes, but large repositories work best with targeted analysis by directory, feature, or service.

faq.question: Will it read secret files?
faq.answer: It should avoid reading real environment files and should use examples or presence checks instead.

faq.question: What output should I expect?
faq.answer: Expect a Markdown report with overview, stack, architecture, quality metrics, recommendations, risk areas, and next steps.

faq.question: Which tools can use this skill?
faq.answer: The report declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.
